nodes.label: actor-ts project snapshot
nodes.rationale: A pre-1.0 actor-model framework for TypeScript running on Bun, Node >= 24 and Deno; ESM throughout with Bun as the primary toolchain. Runtime dependencies are deliberately tiny - fastify plus ts-pattern - and everything else (Express, Hono, ws, brokers, SQL/Cassandra drivers, S3) is an optional peer dependency, lazy-loaded on demand.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits convention
nodes.rationale: type(scope): subject with feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, test, ci, build; scope is the module or area. The body explains what and why plus the mechanics for non-trivial changes, referencing issues as #NNN. Commits touching only CI-maintained artifacts carry [skip ci].

nodes.label: Small, focused commits
nodes.rationale: Each commit keeps bun run typecheck and bun test green, so a bisect never lands on a broken tree.

nodes.label: Commit identity pinned via environment variables
nodes.rationale: Something in the tooling has been observed substituting a work address at commit time, and a wrong author only surfaces afterwards in the log, so the identity is pinned explicitly rather than trusted to config - environment variables outrank both --local config and -c user.email. The values are read back out of git config so the address stays out of the file and the recipe works unchanged in a fork. Applies to merge commits; verify with git log --format='%an <%ae> | %cn <%ce>' -1, since checking git config proves nothing. Nothing is pushed by the agent, so a wrong author is fixable by a mixed reset, re-commit, and comparing the resulting tree hash.

nodes.label: develop / main / features branching model
nodes.rationale: develop is the integration branch and main holds releases only, moving solely on a release merge. All work happens on one features/... branch per unit of work branched off develop - fixes and chores included - with no direct commits to develop; the branch is deleted after it merges. The sole exception is a release/vX.Y.Z branch. main is branch-protected, requiring a PR and the test check, with admin bypass for the release merge.

nodes.label: Always merge --no-ff, never rebase
nodes.rationale: Holds in both directions - features into develop and, at release time, develop into main - so history stays a true graph and is never rewritten or flattened.

nodes.label: Agent commits locally, never pushes
nodes.rationale: The agent commits on its features branch and when merging into develop; the human pushes develop. The single exception is cutting a release, where merging develop into main and creating the tag and GitHub Release is explicitly authorized.

nodes.label: Pre-1.0 SemVer release strategy
nodes.rationale: patch 0.x.Y is bug fixes only; minor 0.X.0 is features and MAY include breaking changes; 1.0.0 is the API-stability commitment. Tags are vX.Y.Z and GitHub Releases are cut as normal Latest releases, not pre-releases. Cutting one: a release/vX.Y.Z branch bumps package.json and dates the CHANGELOG section, merges --no-ff into develop, then develop merges --no-ff into main, then gh release create --target main with emoji-sectioned notes. Publishing triggers publish.yml, which is version-guarded so re-running is safe; locally prepublishOnly runs clean, build, typecheck and test.

nodes.label: Keep a Changelog CHANGELOG
nodes.rationale: An [Unreleased] section with Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed / Security subsections, issues referenced as #NNN, and breaking changes flagged prominently with a BREAKING marker plus a short migration note.

nodes.label: Pre-1.0 breaking changes are a hard cut
nodes.rationale: Remove or replace an API directly - no deprecation cycle is required. Flag it BREAKING in the CHANGELOG with a one-line migration note and update every in-repo caller (examples, tests, docs, benchmarks) in the same change. Post-1.0 this tightens to conservative SemVer.

nodes.label: Bilingual Starlight documentation
nodes.rationale: Docs are Starlight MDX under docs/src/content/docs/ (English) mirrored 1:1 under de/ (German); every content change updates BOTH languages with identical code samples and translated prose, tracked by the i18n label. Feature or behaviour changes also update README.md and CHANGELOG.md, and a new page keeps docs/scripts/scaffold.mjs and the Astro sidebar in sync with the same path and label.

nodes.label: Bot-maintained README test and coverage badges
nodes.rationale: A CI workflow pushes chore(readme): update test count + coverage stats [skip ci] straight to develop after test runs, so the numbers are never hand-edited: the bot overwrites them with CI-measured values that skip the quarantined multi-node suites, which is why they differ slightly from a local full run. After pushing develop, fetch again before branching - a bot commit may already have landed on top.

nodes.label: Pre-commit verification gates
nodes.rationale: Before every commit: bun run typecheck (build tsconfig, excluding examples/tests/benchmarks), bun run typecheck:dev (the same compile plus those three trees), and a green bun test with a line-coverage floor of 80% via bun run test:coverage:gate. Cross-runtime smoke, the examples runner, benchmark compile/smoke, the DevTools UI build check and the audit gate attach to the areas they cover.

nodes.label: typecheck:dev caller-side gate
nodes.rationale: Green since #540 and gated by its own workflow, so a regression is a red check rather than a number that drifts. It is the only gate that sees the library from a CALLER's side, a whole class of defect on its own: an exported class narrower than the interface it implements still satisfies implements, and an exported type whose properties are all optional is satisfied by nothing. Neither shows up in bun test (which transpiles without checking) or bun run typecheck (which never compiles a call site). tsconfig.dev.json excludes only the three trees whose imports another manifest resolves; adding to that list is not a way to make a compile error go away - the rule is a different manifest, not a difficult error.

nodes.label: 80% line-coverage floor
nodes.rationale: bun run test:coverage:gate enforces the same floor locally that CI enforces, so the badge shows what the gate measures.

nodes.label: Three suites that never run in CI
nodes.rationale: ACTOR_TS_SKIP_FLAKY_MNS=1 in test.yml, multi-runtime.yml and publish.yml skips LeaseMajority, ParallelPubSub and ParallelMultiNodeSpec: Bun on GitHub's hosted runners cannot respawn functional worker threads after the first worker test, which also starves LeaseMajority's lease arbitration into a false split-brain. A local bun test runs them; a green CI check says nothing about them. nightly-flakes.yml runs them with the flag off and its header carries the 14-consecutive-green-nights exit criterion, restated in prose in the diagnosing-flakes doc (#538).

nodes.label: Repeat-run flake hunting
nodes.rationale: bun run test:stress loops the suite N times and aggregates failures by test identity, splitting flaky (failed in some runs) from consistently failing (broken, not flaky). It drops ACTOR_TS_SKIP_FLAKY_MNS from the child environment by default, because a harness that inherited it would report a reliable pass rate over exactly the tests known not to be reliable. Not a per-commit gate - reach for it when a test fails intermittently or a nightly names one (#290).

nodes.label: Cross-runtime smoke suite
nodes.rationale: bun run smoke runs tests/smoke/cases/*.mjs on Bun, Node and Deno, and anything runtime-sensitive needs a case. A case must release every handle it opens on EVERY path, not just the happy one: a socket abandoned on a timeout or an error keeps Deno's event loop alive and the run hangs after its last green line without an exit code, so the gate stops being a gate (#1196). The runner's watchdog demotes that to a warning after 15 s but does not excuse it; deno test -A --trace-leaks names the op.

nodes.label: examples.manifest.json classification gate
nodes.rationale: bun run test:examples spawns every runnable snippet and asserts on its output (~90 s); every standalone example is classified as runnable with an output substring that must appear, or skipped with the reason it cannot run. The runner fails when manifest and tree disagree in either direction, so a new example is not finished until it has an entry. The output assertion is not decoration: exited 0 is also what grpc-sensor.ts does after ten failed actor starts, so a runnable case without an expect would gate on nothing. Bun only - the cross-runtime question belongs to smoke.

nodes.label: Benchmark compile and smoke gates
nodes.rationale: A src/ API change that benchmarks/ calls needs bun run typecheck:bench and, for anything that could break at runtime, bun run bench:smoke (~30 s, every suite, one unwarmed iteration). The build tsconfig excludes benchmarks/, so nothing else catches an orphaned benchmark; benchmarks are part of the adoption sweep for a breaking change exactly like tests and examples.

nodes.label: DevTools UI regeneration gate
nodes.rationale: A devtools-ui/ change needs bun run build:ui in the same commit - src/devtools/generated/UiAssets.ts is generated but committed, and a stale one is valid TypeScript so nothing else notices. bun run check:ui asserts it by comparing a source-hash over the UI sources, the build script and the bundled dependencies, deliberately not the bundle's bytes, which vary with OS and Bun release. That means review is the only thing that ever looks at the embedded payload, which is why .gitattributes gives UiAssets.ts a plain textual diff: restoring -diff would remove the last check on those bytes, and the git show noise it saves has per-clone fixes.

nodes.label: CI-side security scanning with one local half
nodes.rationale: bun run lint:audit is bun audit --audit-level=high over bun.lock and gates package-health.yml; run it after any dependency change. It reads the lockfile deliberately - GitHub's dependency graph resolves only the ranges in package.json, so Dependabot and dependency-review-action are blind to the shipped closure and are not used as gates. Advisories predating the gate are suppressed by ID in the script AND listed in SECURITY.md, with SecurityPolicy.test.ts failing if the two sets differ, so one is never silenced without the other. CodeQL and the workflow-hygiene invariants are the rest of it.

nodes.label: Workflow-hygiene invariants
nodes.rationale: tests/unit/ci/WorkflowHygiene.test.ts asserts SHA-pinned actions, explicit read-only workflow permissions and frozen installs, because nothing else in the toolchain reads these files. A new workflow file has to satisfy that test on the first bun test.

nodes.label: Runtime portability through src/runtime abstractions
nodes.rationale: Code must run on Bun, Node >= 24 and Deno; runtime-specific primitives (HTTP serve, sockets, workers, SQLite) live behind small abstractions in src/runtime/ that auto-detect at startup.

nodes.label: Optional peer dependency protocol
nodes.rationale: import() them lazily with a clear install it with bun add ... error on failure; declare them in peerDependencies AND peerDependenciesMeta.<pkg>.optional = true, and add a matching devDependency so the test suite can exercise them.

nodes.label: Every match arm delegates to a private onXxx handler
nodes.rationale: Wherever a ts-pattern match dispatches an incoming message, event or command - onReceive/onCommand/onEvent, a cluster-event subscription, a wire or system-command dispatcher - every .with(...) and any .otherwise(...) is a thin call into a private method, never an inline body, not even a one-liner. Named on + the PascalCase discriminant, parameter typed as the named variant type or omitted for payload-free kinds. It keeps the matcher a scannable dispatch table. Exempt: matches on internal state (state machine, behavior, directive reducer) and matches that compute a value in a helper (config, codec, route, priority).

nodes.label: interface for contracts, type for everything else
nodes.rationale: A declaration is an interface when it prescribes function heads - any method, call or construct signature - or when it extends another shape; everything else is a type alias: plain data shapes, unions, mapped and conditional types. The split follows what the declaration is for: an interface states a contract someone implements and extends reads as a hierarchy where an intersection only reads as conjunction, while a data shape states a value's layout and type composes with the union aliases the project already uses. A function-typed property is not a function head, so that shape stays a type; an interface may extend a type alias, so a contract on a plain data base is interface X extends XBase with XBase staying a type.

nodes.label: Discriminated unions as named variant types
nodes.rationale: Each tagged union is a union of NAMED members, never an inline object-literal union, including the union alias itself (type Command, not type Cmd). A variant is PascalCase(kind) plus a role suffix matching the union (Command/Event/Message) so it is collision-safe, kept module-local with the union. Handlers take the named variant type, not Extract<Union, { kind }>.

nodes.label: The discriminant field is always kind
nodes.rationale: Never type or tag, including the WebSocket and wire protocols of the examples: type collides with the type keyword, and kind is the single project-wide convention.

nodes.label: Pass the actor class, not a closure around it
nodes.rationale: Every ActorClassOrFactory slot - spawn/spawnAnonymous, withEntityActor/withActor/withSingletonActor, the entityActor/singletonActor/actor/child fields, the Router routee - takes the class directly; actorFactoryOf does the wrapping. spawn(() => new MyActor(), 'x') is a leftover from the Props era and reads as noise. The factory form is for constructor arguments and for what the class form cannot express, nothing else; per-actor configuration is the third argument, ActorOptions, never a closure.

nodes.label: Spell out abbreviations in identifiers
nodes.rationale: Types, classes, files, aliases, generic parameters, methods, fields, locals and parameters, plus the kind string-literal values: Command, Message, Acknowledgment, NegativeAcknowledgment, Terminate, Increment, DirectMessage, Request, Response, Function, Context, Connection, Arguments, Directory, Repository, Deduplication, PersistenceId, Implementation, Constructor - not Cmd, Msg, Ack, Nak, Req, Res, Fn, Ctx, Conn, Args, Dir, Repo, Dedup, Pid, Impl, Ctor. Two exceptions only: single-letter loop, lambda and catch variables, and names mirroring an external API or an established domain acronym (nats.js ack/nak, prom-client inc/dec/set, amqplib noAck, DOM AudioContext, MsgPack, PubSub, K8s, AMQP, MQTT, SQL, S3, DNS, CBOR).

nodes.label: JSDoc explains the why
nodes.rationale: Constraints, rationale and non-obvious trade-offs, not a restatement of the code; match the surrounding comment density, no narration or noise.

nodes.label: Typed HOCON keys in ConfigKeys.ts
nodes.rationale: HOCON config keys go through src/config/ConfigKeys.ts as a typed single source of truth. A key in reference.conf must be reachable from ConfigKeys and read by something in src/, or NoDeadConfigKeys.test.ts fails; a knowingly-unimplemented key goes in that test's KNOWN_DEAD_KEYS with the issue that will remove it, and adding a key nothing reads is not an option. That test matches ConfigKeys.<group> and .<leaf> in the SAME file, so relocating a reader breaks it even when behaviour is identical - and bun run typecheck cannot see that failure.

nodes.label: Explicit options > HOCON > built-in defaults
nodes.rationale: Layered with mergeOptions from src/util/OptionsMerge.ts, where undefined on a higher layer means not set and falls through rather than shadowing. The builder or plain object feeds only the highest-precedence explicit layer; unset fields fall through to HOCON, then built-in defaults.

nodes.label: Four-place rule for module-level constants
nodes.rationale: Checked in order, first match wins: (1) XOptions.ts when it is a built-in default or a bound its validator checks; (2) it stays where it is, for a closed list of six kinds - wire/format vocabulary that IS the codec beside it, algorithm-derived sizes fixed by a primitive chosen in that file, a regex or lookup table that is the implementation, a singleton or sentinel needing a class or symbol from the same file, a value derived from another constant in the same file, and protocol declarations in a *Frames.ts; (3) src/<subsystem>/Constants.ts for every other tuned value, one file per top-level directory with nested directories folding up; (4) src/util/Constants.ts only when two or more top-level subsystems consume it, since src/util has no outward import. A Constants.ts imports nothing from its own subsystem, so it is cycle-free by construction - the same property XOptions.ts has. Rule 3 is what rule 1 cannot express: a default shared by two options types has no single XOptions.ts to sit in. Move declarations with their JSDoc verbatim and carry as const and explicit annotations across, or a pure move silently widens a type. Naming is DEFAULT_<DOMAIN>_<UNIT> with the unit suffix, vendor limits prefixed by vendor. Public names stay public because barrels re-export.

nodes.label: One XOptions.ts with three exports
nodes.rationale: Every configurable thing has one XOptions.ts exporting XOptionsType (the plain shape), XOptionsBuilder (fluent, extending OptionsBuilder or BrokerOptionsBuilder) and XOptions, which is BOTH the accepted-input union type and a const value alias to the builder so XOptions.create() resolves. There is no separate Settings concept. Naming is in lockstep with no divergence: builder method withX, field x, HOCON leaf x. All option-relevant types are co-located there; the functional file imports the contracts type-only and never the reverse, so the value edge only runs one way and there is no runtime cycle.

nodes.label: Optional XOptionsValidator fourth export
nodes.rationale: Added when options have real constraints (ports, positive durations or counts, byte sizes, enums, non-empty strings or arrays, URLs, cross-field rules); options that are all booleans, strings or callbacks get none. Helpers take only the field name, typo-checked against XOptionsType, and are a no-op on undefined, so an unset optional always passes and required-ness stays where it was. Validation runs ONCE at consume time on the merged settings, so the builder, a plain object and HOCON are all covered and cross-field rules see final values; it is a separate void assertion, not a resolve helper, and OptionsBuilder has no set-time validation. Rejections throw OptionsError, distinct from BrokerOptionsError and ConfigError.

nodes.label: A builder is structurally its settings
nodes.rationale: OptionsBuilder.set writes each field as an own enumerable property, so an instance is a bag of the fields you set while withX and build stay on the prototype and never surface when spread or serialized. Consumers take the XOptions union and read the argument directly - there is no resolve helper. Keep the union in the signature: a methods-only builder is not assignable to a bare XOptionsType because of the TS weak-type check. Broker actors need nothing, since BrokerActor's constructor takes the union and snapshots it; a subclass that chains builder methods on its parameter must type it XOptionsBuilder, because the union has no methods.

nodes.label: Builder-first documented style
nodes.rationale: Docs and examples show the builder; the plain object is the shorthand alternative, mentioned once per page and never leading. Never nest a builder into a call - assign it to its own contextual local first, then pass the variable. Chains with two or more .withX() calls go one per line; a single .withX() stays on one line, since forcing a lone call onto its own line reads worse.

nodes.label: Issue-first workflow
nodes.rationale: Before starting work, check for an existing issue and work against it, taking its discussion into account; if none exists, open one first for traceability using the matching template in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/. Open an issue before non-trivial work to align on the approach first.

nodes.label: Close issues via the commit body
nodes.rationale: A Closes #NNN line resolves the issue once the commit reaches the repository's DEFAULT branch - here develop, not main - so it closes on the next develop push rather than at release time. There is no release window in which to reconsider, so the line is only added when the work is genuinely finished.

nodes.label: Comment on the issue when the work changes course
nodes.rationale: A new comment as you find it, not an edit to the body, so the sequence stays readable. The commit message records what was done and why and is a poor place for what turned out to be wrong on the way there, and it is invisible to anyone reading the issue later. Worth a comment: the report is inaccurate or stale; the obvious fix does not work (Object.assign reintroducing a prototype-pollution bug verbatim, because it is [[Set]] too); a bound, default or name changed after measuring, with the numbers; the scope moved to another layer, seam, API change or issue; and above all a verification step that proved nothing, which matters more than the result it produced. Same reasoning as issue-first: a duplicate, a wrong severity or an abandoned fix is worth more written down than re-derived.

nodes.label: Label taxonomy
nodes.rationale: priority: {high,medium,low}, severity: {critical,high,medium,low}, security, i18n, infrastructure, dependencies, production-goal, plus standard bug / enhancement / documentation. Audit-catalog items use the title prefixes [Security] and [Feature].

nodes.label: production-goal as a gate, not a batch marker
nodes.rationale: It marks the path to production readiness, so it belongs on any issue that blocks or defines that path regardless of which review found it, including ones filed long before. Filtering on it should answer what is still between us and running this for real, which is why it is applied to existing issues rather than duplicating them.

nodes.label: Security-first posture
nodes.rationale: Cap untrusted input such as WebSocket and wire-frame sizes, never trust client-supplied integrity fields, and use crypto-grade randomness for wire identifiers. A security-relevant change gets a Security CHANGELOG entry and a severity: label.
